transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time today. 

Um, well, my family thought I should come talk to you. I guess... I just don't seem to have the push I used to have. For my choir, or my quilting, or going out visiting folks. I know I should go, and I feel just awful about it because I know people are expecting me. But most days I just end up sitting at home with the TV on real low. 

It's probably just me getting a little older and slower, you know? I don't want you to think I'm just being lazy or giving up, I really do try to be good. Is... is that the sort of thing you needed to know?
When did you first start noticing that you didn't have the energy or motivation to do these activities you enjoyed? Was it a gradual change over months, or did it happen more suddenly?

Oh, well, it certainly wasn't all at once. I wouldn't just stop doing my hobbies and things out of the blue, you know? I always try to keep up with my responsibilities, I really do. 

I suppose... um, it's just been building up slowly. Really, I think it started right around the time I retired from the school office. That was a little over two years ago now. It just sort of snuck up on me, bit by bit since then, just feeling a little more tired each month until I just couldn't seem to get out the door. 

Does... does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it right for you.
Over these past two years, how has your sleep been? Are you sleeping more, less, or about the same as you used to?

Oh, my sleep? Well... I suppose it's been about the same, really. I haven't noticed much of a difference, to be honest with you. 

I always try to make sure I get up at a decent hour every morning. I don't want to just lay in bed all day and waste the day away, you know? I try to keep a proper schedule, just like I always have, even if I don't end up going out much. I'd hate for anyone to think I'm just sleeping my days away. 

So... I'd say it's about the same as it used to be. I hope that's a helpful answer? I'm trying to remember as best I can for you.
Over these past two years, have you been experiencing a lot of worry or anxiety about things? Or would you say the main thing you're dealing with is more just a lack of motivation and low mood?

Oh, um... well, no, I wouldn't say I've been terribly worried or anxious about things. I mean, I worry a little bit, like any mother or grandmother would, just hoping everyone is healthy and doing well. But not... not anything out of the ordinary, I don't think. I try very hard not to be a burden or a fuss-budget, you know? 

I really think it's mostly just... just that lack of push, like you said. The motivation just isn't there, and I feel a bit down about not keeping up with my things. But I don't want to sound like a complainer. I know I have a lot to be thankful for. 

Is... is it okay that I don't feel anxious? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of information.
When you think about your life now, do you feel sad or down in your mood most days? Or would you say your mood is okay, it's just that nothing seems enjoyable or worth doing anymore?

Oh, um... well, I wouldn't say I feel sad, exactly. I don't want you to think I'm sitting around crying all day or anything like that. I really do try to keep a positive outlook, I promise. 

I suppose... it's more like what you said second. Just that... flat feeling, where things don't seem to have the same spark they used to. I don't feel terribly down or depressed, I just... I just can't seem to find the joy in my little projects anymore. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound ungrateful for the life I have. Does that make sense, how I'm explaining it? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of how things are.

Besides the lack of motivation and that flat feeling you described, have you been experiencing any physical symptoms or health problems that have been bothering you? Things like pain, fatigue, headaches, or other physical complaints?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say I've had any real problems like that. I mean, at my age, you get the occasional little ache or pain, maybe a little tiredness if I've been on my feet too long, but nothing... nothing that really bothers me or keeps me from doing what I need to do. 

I really try to take good care of myself, you know? I eat right and try to keep moving, so I don't want you to think I'm falling apart or anything. I've been very blessed with good health, overall. 

So, no, no bad headaches or terrible fatigue or anything like that. I hope that's alright? I just wouldn't want to make a fuss over every little twinge when I know so many people have it much worse.

When you think about your body and your health these days, do you find yourself paying a lot of attention to any particular physical sensations or symptoms, even if they're small things? Or do you mostly just not think much about your health?

Oh, well... no, I mostly just try not to think too much about it. I mean, I do my best to take care of myself, but I'm not... I don't sit around looking for things to be wrong, if that makes sense. 

I know some folks my age can get a bit... well, overly focused on every little tickle or bump, but I really try not to be like that. I just go about my day and leave well enough alone. I don't want to be a bother to anyone, especially not the doctors, by bringing up every little thing. 

I hope that's the right way to look at it? I just figure if I don't pay it too much mind, I won't turn into a complainer. Did I answer that right for you?
Do you find yourself thinking a lot about your health or your body during the day, even when you're trying to focus on other things? Or do these thoughts not really come up much for you?

Oh, well... kind of like I was just mentioning, I really don't let those kinds of thoughts come up much at all. I try to just keep my mind on other things, you know? Just keeping busy around the house, mostly. 

I don't sit and dwell on my body or worry myself over it when I'm trying to do my chores. I promise I'm not one of those folks who fixates on themselves all day. I try to be very good about just letting things be and staying out of my own head, so to speak. 

I hope I'm explaining that right for you? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the answers you need, since I know we just talked about it a little bit.

When you're sitting at home watching TV, do you find yourself noticing sensations in your body—like your heartbeat, or how you're breathing, or any aches—even if they're minor? Or do these kinds of physical sensations just not really catch your attention?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say I notice things like that. When I'm watching my programs, I'm just... well, I'm just watching my programs. 

I'm not sitting there listening to my own heart beating or anything strange like that. I just relax in my chair and enjoy the show. I don't pay any mind to my breathing or little aches. I try to just be normal, you know? Just a regular lady enjoying her evening. 

I hope that's okay to say? I just don't want you to think I'm sitting around obsessing over myself when I should just be enjoying a nice television show. I'm doing my best to just be... well, normal. Is that the kind of thing you were asking about?

You mentioned feeling awful about not keeping up with your choir and visiting, and that you try very hard to be good. Do you find yourself feeling guilty or blaming yourself for not having the energy to do these things? Or do you mostly just see it as something that's happened to you?

Oh, goodness, no... I don't think I blame myself. I mean, I do miss the singing and the visiting, sure, but I know I'm just... well, I'm just not quite up to it right now, and that's just how it is. 

I don't sit around feeling guilty or... or feeling sorry for myself. I really try hard not to be that kind of person who wallows, you know? I just sort of accept it as something that's happened to me for the time being, and I take it one day at a time. 

I hope that's the right attitude to have? I just want to make sure I'm looking at it the right way so I'm not making a fuss or being difficult about it. Did I explain that okay?

I've noticed you've mentioned several times that you hope you're explaining things right and that you don't want me to think poorly of you. How much of your day do you spend worrying about what other people think of you or whether you're being a burden to them?

Oh, my... I didn't mean to give you the wrong impression. I really don't spend my days fretting over what folks think of me, I promise. 

I just... well, since I'm here with you, and you're the doctor, I just want to make sure I'm being a good patient and giving you the right answers. Out in my regular day, I don't sit around worrying about being a burden to anybody. I just try to keep to myself, stay out of the way, and be pleasant and no trouble at all. 

I really hope I haven't been bothersome by asking if I'm doing it right... I just respect your time, is all, and I want to be helpful. I'm not a worrywart, honestly. Does that make sense?
Over these past two years, have there been days or weeks where you felt noticeably sad or down in your mood, even if just for part of the day?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say I've felt sad or down... not really. I mean, sure, everyone has a quiet afternoon now and then, but I don't get sad like that. 

I try to stay positive, you know? I just count my blessings and keep a smile on my face. I wouldn't want to go around being gloomy or making anyone else feel bad because of my mood. I just try to be a cheerful person, even if things are a little slow. 

I hope that's the kind of answer you were looking for? I just want you to know I'm not the type to sit around moping or feeling sorry for myself. I try to be good about things. Is that alright?

Over these past two years since you retired, have there been any stretches of time—maybe weeks or a few months—where you felt more like your old self, with your normal energy and interest in your activities coming back? Or has it been pretty much the same flat feeling the whole time?

Well... I suppose it's just been about the same the whole time. I haven't really noticed any... any stretches where I was suddenly full of energy again. But I wouldn't want you to think I'm just sitting around feeling flat, either. That sounds so dreary, doesn't it? 

I just... I just think of it as being settled. Taking things slow and steady since I retired. I haven't really had my old pep back, no, but I'm doing alright with how things are. It's just been a quiet sort of routine for the past couple of years without much changing. 

I hope that's an okay answer? I just want to be honest with you without sounding like I'm complaining about being tired. I'm really not trying to be difficult about it, I promise. Did that make sense?
Over these past two years, have there been any times when you felt unusually energetic, more talkative than normal, or like you needed less sleep than usual—even if just for a few days?

Oh, heavens no. I haven't had anything like that. I wouldn't want you to think I'm the sort of person who gets all wound up and chatters away, or stays up all hours of the night. 

I've always been a good sleeper, and I try to just keep a nice, even keel, you know? I don't think I've ever had a time where I was bouncing off the walls or talking a mile a minute. I just try to be polite and listen more than I talk. 

I hope that's alright? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of how I am. I'm really just a quiet sort of person, not one to make a fuss or get carried away. Is that the kind of thing you were asking about?

You mentioned things have been pretty much the same flat feeling for the whole two years since you retired. During those two years, was there ever a stretch of even a week or two where you felt more like yourself—where you had more interest in things or felt a bit more like your normal self—before it went back to feeling flat again?

Oh... no, I don't believe so. I haven't really had a week or two where things felt different like that. It's just been... well, very steady, I suppose. 

I know you used the word 'flat,' and I hope I didn't make it sound like I'm just wasting away or being lazy about my days. I really do try my best to keep my chin up and be good. It's just that my interest in things hasn't really bounced back or changed at all, it's just stayed this quiet way for the whole time since I stopped working. 

I hope that's an okay answer? I want to make sure I'm giving you what you need for your notes... am I explaining it alright for you?

When you think back over these two years since you retired, even if just for a day or two here and there, have there been any times when your mood felt a little bit better or lighter than usual—maybe when you were doing something pleasant or spending time with family?

Well... I mean, I suppose if my sister comes over for a cup of tea, I try to be pleasant and put on a smile for her. I wouldn't want to bring anyone else down, you know? But... I wouldn't say my mood actually feels any lighter or better inside. It's just... I just try to be good company. 

Even when something nice is happening, that quiet, settled feeling just sort of stays exactly where it is. I hope that doesn't make me sound ungrateful for my family's visits. I really do appreciate them, I just... the feeling inside doesn't really shift. 

Is that the right kind of thing to tell you? I just want to be sure I'm answering you properly without sounding like a sourpuss. I try my best to be cheerful for others, I really do. Did I explain that okay?

During these two years since you retired, has there been any stretch of time—say two months or longer—where you felt back to your normal self, where things felt like they used to before all this started?

Oh, no... I don't think so. I haven't had a time like that, where things went back to how they used to be for two whole months. It's just been the same quiet way this whole time. 

I hope that's alright to say. I don't want you to think I'm not trying to get better or that I'm just giving up. I try very hard every day to keep things nice and tidy, and to be good. It's just... the feeling inside hasn't really changed back to normal for any long stretch like that. 

I'm sorry if that's not the answer you were hoping for. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information. Am I doing okay?

I want to make sure I haven't missed anything. Looking back over these two years, even if it was just for a few days, has there ever been a time when you felt more energetic or more interested in doing things than you do now—a time when you had more of your old spark, even if it didn't last very long?

Oh, well... no, I don't believe so. I really wish I could tell you yes, because I know that would be much better news for you to write down. But no, I haven't really felt that old spark or had a burst of energy like that. 

I do make sure to get up and do my chores every morning, though—I'm definitely not just laying in bed all day, I promise you that. I keep the house nice and clean, and I do my best. It's just that the extra energy or interest to do much else hasn't really come back. 

I'm sorry if I'm just repeating the same sort of thing over and over for you... I just want to be completely honest so you have what you need. Am I doing alright with all these questions?
